description: Required, one or more MeasurementObservation members. Each member is a complete MeasurementObservation (observation_type, value_quantity, body_position, context, qualifier and so on, see MeasurementObservation Metadata); the set adds nothing but grouping. The Members column of the Concepts file lists the member concepts by their MeasurementObservation concept name; a source that lacks one member still gets the set with the members it has. One set per participant per visit per test session (for blood pressure, one set per reading or per average).
Example source variable description: [Computed net average of second and third blood pressure measurement]. 2nd and 3rd systolic. Q21 [Siting Blood Pressure. SBPA. Visit 1]|[Third blood pressure measurement]. 2nd and 3rd diastolic. Q22 [Siting Blood Pressure. SBPA. Visit 1]

description: Optional on the set in BDC-HM (required on each member). Gold fills it on the set and on every member from the same participant identifier.

Optional in BDC-HM. Fill it on the set so all members share one visit: the visit is derived from the source visit or exam variable, never from the member value. Where a table holds several visits (SPIROMICS VISIT, COPDGene P1/P2/P3), derive the visit with a case expression on that variable.
Optional free string for the general category of the set. Not used by gold; leave blank unless a downstream grouping is agreed.
Optional, multivalued: the entity directly measured. Not used by gold; leave blank.

Optional, multivalued string for the method used to generate the whole set. Gold does not set it on sets; method is recorded per member on MeasurementObservation.method_type (for example 'spirometry', 'calculated', 'Seated random-zero average'). Do not set it on the set unless every member shares the method.
Optional Organization that performed the set (for example a reading center). Not used by gold; leave blank.
There is NO observation_type or CURIE on a set in BDC-HM or in gold; the set is identified by the observation_type codes of its members. Do not invent a set-level code.

Bronchodilator status is carried per member, not per set. Each spirometry member gets one Context with Activity activity_type BRONCHODILATOR_MEDICATION_USE and relative_timing BEFORE (pre-bronchodilator) or AFTER (post-bronchodilator); this is what gold does for COPDGene (BEFORE and AFTER), HCHS/SOL (BEFORE only), SPIROMICS and LTRC. The bronchodilator status is also in the concept name ('FEV1 post bronchodilator'); keep both and see questions. For a set where every member shares a timing, repeat the same Context on every member. A member whose source does not state bronchodilator status gets no bronchodilator Context: no Context means unknown, never assume pre-bronchodilator. Predicted (reference-equation) values carry no bronchodilator Context because they are not measured; percent-predicted values inherit the status of the measured value they are computed from and carry the same Context. ARIC gold records pre/post only in method_type text (Pre-bronchodilator, spirometry), which is not Context.

Spirometry taken before the bronchodilator (pre-bronchodilator). Use on every member of the pre-bronchodilator set and on any spirometry member whose source says pre-bronchodilator (for example COPDGene FEV1_pre in the shared spirometry file).
Example source variable description: Pre-bronchodilator Forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1)

description: Spirometry taken after the bronchodilator (post-bronchodilator). Use on every member of the post-bronchodilator set and on any spirometry member whose source says post-bronchodilator (for example COPDGene FEV1_post in the shared spirometry file).
Value used with Context for spirometry sets; combine with relative_timing BEFORE or AFTER.

Qualifier is set per member. For blood pressure, an average of repeat readings is AVERAGE in BDC-HM, but gold records it today in method_type text ('Seated random-zero average', 'average') and uses qualifier only for spirometry (MAXIMUM, best of the trials: CARDIA, JHS) and sodium. Set it on both systolic and diastolic so the pair stays consistent.

Blood pressure that the source reports as the mean of two or more readings (for example the mean of the second and third sitting readings in ARIC, or the average blood pressure in SPIROMICS). Put it on both systolic and diastolic. State in method_type how many readings were averaged when the source says.
Example source variable description: [Computed net average of second and third blood pressure measurement]. 2nd and 3rd systolic. Q21 [Siting Blood Pressure. SBPA. Visit 1]|Average Systolic Blood Pressure

description: Spirometry value that the source labels the maximum or best of several trials (CARDIA, JHS). Use for FEV1, FVC and the ratio from the best trial; gold records second and third best curves in method_type text.

Blood pressure from the first of a series of readings (for example ARIC First blood pressure measurement). Gold currently records these as method_type 'Seated random-zero reading'; keep the reading number in method_type and use this qualifier only if Anne approves (see questions).
Example source variable description: [First blood pressure measurement]. 1st systolic. Q12 [Siting Blood Pressure. SBPA. Visit 1]

description: Blood pressure and spirometry in the cohorts here are taken seated; use SITTING_POSITION on every member. Use SUPINE_BODY_POSITION for supine readings (gold does for ankle-brachial blocks).
Example source variable description: [Computed net average of second and third blood pressure measurement]. 2nd and 3rd systolic. Q21 [Siting Blood Pressure. SBPA. Visit 1]

description: Blood pressure: set the arm on both members. BDC-HM models body_site as a BodySite with a required Uberon-based site and an optional qualifier (laterality, for example right); gold today writes the string 'Right arm' (ARIC, CHS, SPIROMICS, others) and 'Left arm' where a source says so. Leave blank when the source does not say which arm. Spirometry has no body site.

Per member. Blood pressure: the device and the reading, as gold writes it ('Seated random-zero average', 'Seated random-zero reading', 'Omron automated average', 'oscillometric cuff', 'auscultatory method', 'average'). Spirometry: 'spirometry' for measured values, 'calculated' for ratios derived by the cohort, and the reference equation for predicted values (COPDGene writes 'Hankinson').

Each member keeps the code of its MeasurementObservation concept. Gold uses OMOP:4152194 (systolic) and OMOP:4154790 (diastolic), and for spirometry OMOP:4241837 (FEV1), OMOP:4176265 (FVC), OMOP:3011505 (FEV1/FVC), OMOP:3022891 / OMOP:3002094 / OMOP:3024594 (predicted FEV1 / FVC / FEV1/FVC), OMOP:3011708 / OMOP:3005600 / OMOP:4196583 (percent predicted FEV1 / FVC / FEV1/FVC). The OMOP label of OMOP:4196583 is 'FEV1/FVC percent', not percent predicted; the HM enum text and production use it as percent predicted (see questions). See questions: gold uses these plain codes for post-bronchodilator members too.

Units are per member. Blood pressure mm[Hg]; volumes L; FEV-family ratios (FEV1/FVC and its predicted and post-bronchodilator forms, FEV1/FEV6, FEV3/FEV6, FEV3/FVC) use % (0-100): ratio-form sources (0-1) are multiplied by 100, as gold does and as the MeasurementObservation Concepts target unit says; percent predicted %.
Integer days (BDC-HM). Where the source gives age in years, gold uses years x 365, the same expression on every member of the set.

Do not pool blood pressure across cohorts without the protocol. ARIC and CHS used a random-zero sphygmomanometer (ARIC SBPA21/SBPA22 are the mean of the 2nd and 3rd of three sitting readings); other cohorts use automated oscillometric devices or the mean of different reading numbers. Random-zero and oscillometric values can differ by several mm[Hg], so keep device and averaging in method_type and qualifier. Blood pressure is also confounded by antihypertensive treatment: pair with the treatment concept when comparing. The blood_pressure file also holds ankle-brachial and carotid blocks, which are not part of this set. The device can also change between exams within a cohort (ARIC moved from random-zero to automated oscillometric measurement at a later exam; confirm the exam in the ARIC protocol), so record the device per source table in method_type.

Pre- versus post-bronchodilator is the key distinction: airflow obstruction (COPD, GOLD) is defined on post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC below 0.70, so a set with unknown bronchodilator status is not comparable with one that has it. Predicted and percent-predicted values depend on the reference equation (Hankinson/NHANES III is used in COPDGene; GLI-2012 and later race-neutral GLI equations differ, and the 2023 ATS statement (Bhakta et al., AJRCCM 2023, PMID 36973004) recommends race-neutral equations): record the equation in method_type, and do not mix percent predicted from different equations. Acceptability grading and best-of-three selection differ by cohort (CARDIA and JHS report the maximum). Not every cohort measured every volume (FEV0.5, FEV3, FEV6 are rare).
